utterances.text: Do you know anything about that, or did this person really disappear, and if he went missing, what were the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: I don't remember. Zoran Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes. Very well, you don't remember. But Mrs. Badrov, the name Vidovic, is that a frequent name?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Yes, that is a very frequent last name in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And the name Zoran as a first name, given name?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: There are a large number of Zorans.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Look at the next document, please. That would be Z957.1. Will you please review the document and see if you can identify it, see who it was signed by, when it was issued, by whom. Ms. Badrov, will you please focus your attention on -- do you think that this document was issued by the Vitez Brigade and signed by the person who is listed here?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: It seems as if the Deputy Commander of the brigade -- assistant commander signed it, but it looks like an official document that could have been issued by the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: When you look at the header, when you -- actually the heading says, "List of killed, wounded, and missing members of our units for the period." The reference is "our units."

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: We did not use that, that much. We do not have ten units, we only had one, the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You have the distribution. It says Zoran Piletic did you know him?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Yes, I did know Zoran Piletic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Considering the position of Mr. Cilic, his job, would this perhaps provide an answer why this list is being sent to Mr. Piletic?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Perhaps for propaganda reasons, I don't know why else, why he would send such a document to Zoran Piletic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: This would be actually the reference -- in reference to document Z808. Would the contents of this, the contents of this list really be an expanded list contained in Z808?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And again, it -- it's another document drafted by Mr. Cilic?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. How about, let's say, the person listed as number one on the first sheet. Look at his year of birth.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Yes, this is a very old person, the person that is of an age that is beyond the, beyond recruitment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: His name is Anto Kristo. Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: I -- perhaps I did, but I cannot connect the name with the face.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Will you now go to page 3. Again, we're looking at a person listed as number one. Can you recall whether this person was a member of the Vitez Brigade, or perhaps a member of another unit?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Dragan Sapina, I really don't know. But for instance, number 16, Mile Vinac, he was a member of the district -- of the district staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What do you mean by district staff?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: He was in the Hotel Vitez. I actually did have some official contact with him, so that's how I know him. Again, Adis Cosic, son of Abe, again a member of the military police. You see, the same names are cropping up again as in the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. I think we can move on. Next document, Z1372.1. Do you have the Croatian version in front of you?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Will you please look at the date of this document? The heading would refer to which unit that issued this document?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: It seems as if this was issued by the 5th Battalion command. If they issued it, because it is not signed. It is possible that it was an internal document drafted in the battalion, but the 5th Battalion was one of the Vitez Brigade battalions. It says that this is a list of soldiers in the zone of responsibility of the 5th Battalion, but the men listed here did not belong to it at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: One thing that's not clear to me, and let me ask you first this: Do you remember at all when the 5th Battalion of the Vitez Brigade was formed?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: The 5th Battalion? You see, at first we had -- I cannot tell you specifically, but this was towards the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The "zone of responsibility" is used as a military term.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the 5th Battalion did have a zone responsibility in the areas which are listed here as the place of death?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: For instance, the 5th Battalion did have responsibility for the part of the front line at Mahala and adjoining Stari Vitez. So Stari Vitez, yes, this could be part of their zone of responsibility, but Kruscica, not at all. Novaci, perhaps, yes. That could be part of that. So some, yes; some, no. But for instance, Dario Krgovic, he was a member of the work platoon. Yes. It says here SPS, Vitez. He was not part of the brigade and he was not on the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What number is he listed under?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Thirteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Can you identify anyone else? Under 1, we have a person whom we had seen before.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Yes, Zlatko Nakic, for instance. He was a member of the military police. Well, Andrija Krizanac, too. Zoran Cerosi [phoen]. All this is military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Next question. If these men listed here were killed in the zone of responsibility of the 5th Battalion, as it is stated here in the heading, did the command of the unit whose responsibility it was was in charge of registering all the casualties incurred in their zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Yes. They kept a log of anything that went on. Of course, even if a civilian was killed in their zone of responsibility, I believe that they would have registered that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let me just draw your attention to the person under 8, Borislav Jozic. Is that the same person?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Yes. See, the same. He was never a member of the 5th Battalion, but the front line was in the immediate proximity of the place, the location where he was killed. And Franjo Garic. If this is the Franjo Garic that I know, he was killed in his building, which was right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Moving on to the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: How many documents are you going to produce or you're going to have evidence about?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: There are 15 documents in that binder, but I will not go to 13, which is Z1009.1, except -- I will, but only for a small detail, because those are various reports or official records, not the listings which the witness might be familiar with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We shall be finishing at quarter to four today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I will do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Badrov, the next list is Z1324.1. Will you please again look at the heading, look at the signature, and again we see that the brigade police is mentioned. Please look at the date. Can you tell us whether this is an authentic document which indeed could have been drafted by the person who signed it? And who was this person who signed it?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Given the date -- this is December 1993, when some of the military police or the security unit could have been already in existence as part of the Vitez Brigade. However, Ms. Mira Vrebac was a lady who was in charge of the care matters. So it would make no sense for her to do anything with the brigade police. Maybe she was just compiling some list and that was part of that general work that she was engaged in. I'm not clear on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on. We're moving to the document Z505. Witness Cenkic already dealt with this document here, but let me ask you one thing. There's a lot of lists there in English. Unfortunately, not all pages are marked. Then we have -- and then we have -- this is followed by the part in Croatian which is marked as D18/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The one with very small printing is Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you please look at the top right corner, the date, and the header saying who issued this, and the heading. Can you please explain to us what this document could represent? You said at that time, you did not work at the brigade.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: No, I was not there in February. I can only conclude from these headings that this was a battalion, the Vitez battalion, which was part of the Stjepan Tomasevic in Novi Travnik, because I see that MP number code is Novi Travnik. So I don't know if this was a payroll or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Badrov, when you started working at the brigade, did you issue for certain periods, monthly or a weekly basis, lists of people who had served at the front line in various shifts?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In the period between the start of your job at the brigade and the conflict, did you ever produce documents, lists of soldiers who were going to Slatka Voda, Strikanci, in other words, to the shifts facing Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Listen, I told you that at the beginning of the conflict I was engaged in the establishment of the brigade, and the only thing I remember regarding shifts is that one shift was left behind when the conflict broke out and they were pulled back later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. I'm going to ask you to turn to page 3. It is the list of the HVO members from Novi Travnik. This is the 3rd Platoon, 3rd Company of the 2nd Battalion. And please look at the person listed under number 1. Who is this person, please? The name is Ivica Badrov. His registration number --

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Sorry. I don't have the right page. It is something else. Oh, it's page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, page 4.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: This person is my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did your brother go to the front line in one of the shifts while he was at the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Yes. He was going to Slatka Voda, and on the day when the conflict broke out, he happened to be there, and it took him about two days to break through and come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. I think that we've clarified this point. We can move on without wasting time. The next document is Z1009.1. We have dealt with documents produced by the same person. The author of this document is Nihad Rebihic. Let me just ask you about the first person listed in this document. The print is very bad, so can you make it out?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Marko Lujic, son of Marko Anto. I believe that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Couple of questions. Was this person ever a member of the Vitez Brigade throughout your employment there?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: No. He was involved in pyrotechniques. He dealt with explosives, and he was involved in the wartime production throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me who was the head of artillery at that time?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: I believe that it was Damnjan Baskarad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you regarding the next document, but one thing regarding Mr. Rebihic and Mahala. Ms. Badrov, do you know anything about a radio in Vitez known as Radio Mahala?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Yes. I know that it was engaged in propaganda, and it was called Radio Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Ms. Badrov, did you hear whether this radio ever talked about you specifically, Gordana Badrov?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: At that time, I was very busy. I didn't have the time to listen to Radio Mahala. I don't think I was mentioned by name, but I think I was described to -- to sufficient detail to be recognised, to be identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: When -- who asked you about this?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: It was my friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And what did they ask you? What was this about?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: The news item described me as a sniper because I was the only woman wearing a uniform at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Badrov, did you ever carry weapons during that period of war?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: No. I don't believe in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Now, could we move on to the second binder, but there we shall only look at two or three examples. We'll not go through the whole book, as it would take us to the end of the week. I should like to single out only a few examples here. For instance, first section, number 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is the -- the whole file is registered under number Z2813.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at the individual under 16. On the first page of that list, which is Z505, which we already saw, we have the name of two persons circled, under 2 and under 6, Damnjan Baskarad and Goran Baskarad. Mrs. Badrov, could you say on the basis of this document these two men are members of the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: I can't say whether yes or no simply because this document originated before the Vitez Brigade was born, that is, on the 27th of February. And I really don't know. How can I say whether yes or no. The heading of the Vitez Brigade is missing. The Vitez Brigade did not issue it. We have already said that this could be the payroll, for instance, or something that was drawn up for a shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, will you please turn to an individual whose name was frequently mentioned here who figures under number 23. We have already broached that. The name in this section is Miroslav Bralo, called Cicko. Mrs. Badrov, I will read out to you facts from three different birth certificates and would like to -- I will then ask you which one could he be in view of the allegations of the individual under 2 in this list. Now, excuse me, what is it that you have there?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: I have here a report on the wounding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: No. The first list should be Z67, and that's what it looks like. [In English] In binder 23. Why don't you look at the next one, perhaps. They're mixed up there. [Interpretation] Miroslav Bralo called Cicko, that should be the first page. Z67 to see if we are both dealing with the same document. I have three fragments from the registry of births issued to three persons all called Miroslav Bralo. One is the son of Pero born in 1958. Could that be the person under two?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Well, I don't think so because it says here that he was born on the 13th of October, 1967, and he also has the -- his identity number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So it should be the son of Jozo, according to the list?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And according to his identity number, he was born in 1967?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Now, will you look at the next document, Z265.1?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In Croatian, I'm afraid you can't see a thing, but the English is all right. And in English you have the name, and it is recognizable. It is person under one, again the same name, Miroslav Bralo.

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: This is the payroll for the Vitez Alpha Force group. You already saw this document. Here we have no particulars. No, there aren't any. But can we say that it's the same person that we saw on the previous list?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: No. We cannot say whether it is the same person, not from this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: We have already seen this list, we do not have to go back to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder what we're really achieving with this, and what this last passage of examination has been aimed at. If I've understood it, and it's a little difficult to follow, Mr. Kovacic reads out the name of another person with the same name, and the witness says, "Well, it can't be the same person." I don't really know where we're going.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kovacic, what is the point?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The point is, Your Honour, I'm trying to show, and I will later add a couple of documents in our own binder, we're still investigating that, that those documents which were presented by the Prosecution as a base for alleged conclusion, for a possible conclusion that certain persons were members of the brigade at a certain point of time, that it is entirely not reliable, and it cannot serve for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm just building up examples.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, have you got any more?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I will only dwell on just one document more concerning that person, and I think it will be enough. Well, perhaps we could also go to yet another one, but I believe we can use some other examples when we add some documents and then make our point even more emphatic. May I go on? Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Badrov, in the same document, we have document Z1465.4. Mrs. Badrov, you spent your life working with documents, and I should like to ask you first, under the Administrative Proceedings Act, and there is a standard which existed and still exists in the republic of the former Yugoslavia, how does one rectify errors in documents? Will you please tell us what is the standard, what is the law?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: The law requests to rectify documents as it was done here, that is, that the sentence which needs to be rectified or part of the sentence that has to be rectified is crossed out, but it has to be legible. Nevertheless, one has to see what it says, what is crossed out, then below it to write the correction, the rectification, and then initial it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you recognise the initial on the -- the initials on this document?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. And here we have Miroslav Bralo born in 1967 mentioned here, so we guess that this is the same person that we talked about previously. We have some facts about his wounding. And it says that he was wounded on the 19th of September in the area of Krtina Mahala. But in the correction it says -- or rather, before it is corrected it says that he was a member of the defence battalion between the 16th of April, 1993, until the 13th of April, 1994; and then this is corrected and said that it was in the unit from the 7th of September, 1993, until the 19th of September, 1993, that is, until the day when he was wounded according to this. Since you are familiar with the procedure at the time, could you tell us why was this correction made?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Well, I can make a guess. This document was issued in 1995, that is, he evidently wrote to the commander of the Vitez Brigade applying for such a document so as to exercise his right to, to benefits.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And when somebody applies for such a request to such -- who does that?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Well, it's this service which keeps the records, that is the service which has all the information about one's participation in the war, and that is the personnel department. They had this kind of information. In addition to them -- at least that is what the practice was before, I do not know whether it is still valid, but any member of the brigade was to bring along the certificate from the inferior unit, that is, from the 1st Battalion command, to bring a certificate indicating his time of service with that battalion. Now, if the exact date was missing, then in principle one would take three dates, and those three dates you will usually find in such certificates. It is the dates of the September 1991 -- I mean, when -- the date when official -- the date which was officially taken as the date of aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is, the village of Ravno; then April 1992 when the HZ HB was founded; and then the third date, 16th of April when open fighting broke out between the Muslims and Croats. These three dates are, as a rule, taken to mean the beginning of one of the -- of a soldier's involvement for whom we did not have exact information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And if there was accurate information?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: If there was accurate information, then one would put in the accurate information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: A clerk -- so, a clerk who fills in this paper, who does she forward it to?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: The lady clerk who fills in this paper must take it to the commander for initialing. Now, if she is a clerk in a battalion, then she must show it to the battalion commander. If she's a clerk in the brigade command, then she will take it to the brigade commander for initialling.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Presumably this correction was done before it was signed?

utterances.speaker: GORDANA BADROV
utterances.text: Yes, presumably. From what I can conclude from this document, it was issued by the commander of the 1st Battalion. It's also properly signed by the commander of the 1st Battalion; however, it is quite obvious that in the brigade commander [sic] there was the accurate date of the person's involvement, so the 1st Battalion put down the date of the beginning of the conflict. But then when it arrived in the brigade, then in the brigade, they knew the exact date, and they rectified this date pursuant to the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So this is really not unusual?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've had enough now for today, it's quarter to, and I'm going to make a note, and then we'll adjourn. There will be an ex parte hearing. Mrs. Badrov, will you be back, please, at half past nine tomorrow morning to go on with your evidence. How much longer do you think you're likely to be, Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I think tomorrow that I could finish.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, your microphone please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I believe that I could finish tomorrow for about between half an hour and 45 minutes, I'm sure. I will use one example in this file, and then briefly through, through the list for certificates which the Chamber have heard enough, so it's....

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And how many more witnesses have you this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: We are expecting a witness to come this evening, and we will bring this witness tomorrow for testimony, and we are quite uncertain about the said witness, but hopefully he will come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may raise just two short questions, technical --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness go. Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A few days ago the Chamber asked the Prosecution to disclose documents which they intend to use in the cross-examination of the accused Cerkez once he takes the stand. We have not yet received those documents, and of course, we would be very happy if we could see them on time -- in time; otherwise, we shall not be able to go through them. On Sunday, I cannot go to the detention unit; the last day is Saturday, so I should like to ask the Prosecution to disclose them to us as soon as possible. Moreover we have not yet received a translation of the Witness AT's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's deal with that. Mr. Nice can you provide the documents please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The position is, Your Honour, that Your Honour raised it speaking for yourself, as to whether that was a course to be pursued in this matter we wish to discuss it with the Chamber and the Defence, of course, at some stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, what --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In any event, it's wholly unrealistic to think that we are in a position to serve a list of documents. Even if the Chamber were to make such an order or make such a request, we are nowhere near that state of readiness, I have to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps more accurately, make sure that all such documents are disclosed or have been disclosed, that perhaps is a more felicitous way of putting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. But I suspect we're going to run out of evidence before the end of sitting on Thursday, from what I hear from Mr. Kovacic, and I suspect it would be a good idea if we just discussed that topic lightly so that we know where we stand, and we will then be able to comply so far as in our ability.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We will discuss it, but I cannot believe that you intend to try and ambush --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There's a difference between -- can we discuss it at that time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If I may say so, I'm well aware of the cases of certain jurisdiction which touch on this issue, Phillipson and Sansom to name two of them. Yes, I think Mr. Kovacic had something else he wanted to raise. But before we come to that general discussion, whether it's tomorrow or Thursday, I simply observe that we don't yet know the main points upon which Mr. Cerkez is going to be giving evidence. Whether we're entitled to a summary under the rules or not is another issue. Again, I'm not concerned to argue it heavily now, or maybe at any stage, but I observe that in fact we do not know what are the points he's going to touch, so that's something else to be considered when we discuss the issue of the exchange of or the provision of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, what was the other point?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, before that, if I just may answer. If the document will be discovered to us on Thursday or Friday, better to say, then I don't have any use after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think the point is this, and it may be that I was not careful enough in what I said. What I had in mind was that if there were any documents upon which he was to be cross-examined, they should have been documents which should have been disclosed, not that you'd be provided with a list of the documents on which he was going to be cross-examined. You must be taken to know the case and have prepared it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: That is what is your order, we will of course apply it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There's no order at the moment, it's merely a discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If I may raise a third issue --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's deal with them one at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The latest information will be completed, I understand, by tomorrow or Thursday. I will investigate, once we rise, the possibility of disclosing part already in some satisfactory and secure way, and we can communicate with Mr. Kovacic by telephone rather than keep him back, as I'm sure it will take some time even if part of it's ready tonight. If part of it's ready tonight, we can find a way of handing it over subject to the usual terms. What I've asked to have done is to have the usual system -- not the usual system, the same system of watermarking documents, and it seems to me that if they are provided in that way, one copy marked for one defendant and one copy marked for another defendant, that will, I think, probably fall within the provisions of the earlier protective measures, and providing we hand it over in a secure way, that should be satisfactory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If I could raise a third question then. It is the issue of contact of Defence counsel with the accused after he begins with his testimony. There is your order --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I know we have an order. I think that might be a matter which could be more conveniently dealt with when we have more time. You can mention it at the end of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And of course if we run out of evidence, normally we would expect the next part of the evidence, which would be your client's evidence, to begin. You may like to think about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I've no doubt you will have a submission, but we will hear it in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: We gave up some witnesses in order to get additional time to prepare Mr. Cerkez as a witness. Perhaps out of the trial I could inform my colleague about the main topics of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn now and sit in ten minutes, ex parte.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
